hyps.why: With the 0->3 edge already removed, deleting the 2->3 edge often leaves only edge 4 or nothing feeding the output, risking a disconnected or very weak cell.
If 2->3 is absent, removing 0->3 strips one of the few remaining routes into the output node, so the deletion hurts much more.
With 1->3 absent, the output depends on edges 3 and 5 only, so removing edge 3 more often disconnects or bottlenecks the cell.
When edge 0 is none, node 1 receives zero input, so any op on 1->3 contributes nothing and the edit's gain vanishes.
With node 1 zeroed by a none on edge 0, a conv on 1->2 processes nothing, so its usual benefit disappears.
If node 1 has no direct path to the output, a conv on 0->1 only matters through edge 2, so the improvement is diluted.
When 2->3 is none, node 2 is a dead end, so adding a conv on 0->2 has no effect on the output.
Turning an absent 2->3 edge into a conv adds a whole new learned path, a much larger gain than replacing an existing skip or pool.
Adding a residual input-to-output shortcut where none existed greatly improves optimization, whereas replacing a conv on edge 3 with skip gives little or loses capacity.
Replacing the high-value 2->3 conv with a parameter-free pool loses a lot of capacity, whereas putting a pool where an edge was none or skip costs little or helps.
